title: Split reading.rs into submodules to get under 1500 lines
summary: Restructure crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (about 1737 production lines, 8 landings in 7 days) by moving cohesive groups into child modules under crates/athena-core/src/reading/. Candidates are the retry and carry-over helpers, the delivery-verb and outcome-state check, the defined-terms check, and the reference and boundary checks. Public paths stay the same through re-exports. Behavior does not change. The audience is the code-health gate and maintainers.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust code only.
cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
One structural split with no logic changes.
A verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
The test suite is the check for unchanged behavior, plus a diff check that confirms the change is a pure move.
Several cohesive responsibilities move out, so the file stays under the limit and does not creep back over it.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (top-level item outline only) and listed crates/athena-core/src/. The file is declared in lib.rs, and its items are used through crate::reading:: by run/, steward.rs, plan.rs, status.rs, hestia.rs, tests/refusal_corpus.rs and the athena-cli crate. No record or data file is added, so the records allow-list is untouched.

The file has many sections beyond impl Athena: the retry and carry code, the brief-topic code, the check_* functions, the delivery-verb and outcome-state tables, and the defined-terms and quoted-span helpers. Each section is self-contained and can move to its own child module with `pub use` re-exports, so callers do not change.

Converting reading.rs to a module with child files keeps reading.rs as the parent, using Rust's non-mod-rs layout (reading.rs plus reading/*.rs). Only reading.rs is in the request's Files line, so the new child files are the extra deliverables.
Tests that sit in the file's test module may need to stay in the parent or move with their code. Their assertions are not changed.
Code health counts production lines per file. The target is the parent file under 1500 lines, and the children are well under the limits too. No function over 200 lines is introduced.
Environment: none. This is a local refactor with no CI, push or network.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs has fewer than 1500 production lines (test modules excluded). Every new child file under crates/athena-core/src/reading/ is also under 1500 lines, and no function exceeds 200 lines. Check by reading the files.

Every previously public item of crate::reading (for example check_defined_terms, check_outcome_state, plan_entry, earlier_attempt, retry_findings, same_scope) is still reachable at the same path. The diff shows `pub use` re-exports and no edits to callers outside reading.rs, apart from mod declarations.
The diff is a pure move. Function bodies, constants and tests are unchanged apart from visibility (pub(super) or pub(crate)) and import paths. No logic edits.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core`, including tests/refusal_corpus.rs and the reading tests. All pass, with the same tests and no removed or ignored ones.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean, and `cargo build` succeeds for the whole workspace.
athena.toml, defaults.toml and the workflows are not changed. The change is one focused structural split.

out_of_scope: Any behavior change, new check or refusal rule
Changes to callers outside reading.rs beyond what re-exports make unnecessary
Edits to athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflows
departures: A move-only refactor of a 4000-line file risks visibility and import errors, so the cost and time are slightly above the reference. The pass probability is about the same.
